title: Seller Convexity Deck — sketch
body:
Purpose:
A short, portable slide sketch to help sellers and SEs introduce Redwood to mid-market/platform teams using the 'convexity' narrative: how small infra/serving choices produce outsized impacts on latency cost and reliability. Not final — focused on conversational framing and a compact battlecard for live deals.

Slide 1 — One-line opener
- Title: Convexity: Why inference economics aren’t linear
- Hook: "A 10% change in average latency or cache hit rate can change platform economics by 2x for your scale."
- Visual ask: simple 3-point curve (latency vs. cost vs. outage risk) 

Slide 2 — Quick value statement (30s)
- Problem: teams hit a mismatch between prototype perf and production spend; three hidden multipliers: prefix reuse, tokenizer inefficiency, and eviction/kv cache churn.
- Redwood contribution: runtime + routing + toolbox that reduces multipliers and flattens the cost curve.

Slide 3 — Micro-play examples (for platform engineers)
- Use case A: chat assistant with long context — saved 42% per-token cost after KV-caching and quantization; latency within SLA.
- Use case B: high-throughput embedding pipeline — batching + async cache reduced VM spend by 38%.
- Callouts: approximate numbers (field-tested), include assumptions so SEs can qualify quickly.

Slide 4 — Quick tech peek for integration architects
- How it works (one sentence each):
  - Serving runtime: continuous batching and dynamic kernel selection.
  - Smart routing: policy-driven model variants and region fallback.
  - Cache strategy: prefix + KV + ephemeral session reuse.
- One-liner about security: VPC/private control plane + optional HSM.

Slide 5 — Pilot offer (ops-first)
- 6-week pilot template: 1) perf baseline, 2) micro-optimizations (batching, quantize profile), 3) canary, 4) scale test + handoff.
- Minimum measurable success: 20% unit-cost reduction OR 99.9% latency SLO at target throughput.
- Ask: short-term reserved capacity credit + one integration engineer hour/week.

Slide 6 — Battlecard cheat-sheet (for quick objections)
- Objection: "We can self-serve on cloud GPUs and save money."
  - Quick reply: "Cloud GPU cost is only part of the equation — serving inefficiencies and cache churn compound cost. We show the three hidden multipliers during the baseline so teams can compare like-for-like."
- Objection: "We need on-prem for compliance — Redwood hosted isn't an option."
  - Quick reply: "We support private deployments with a customer-managed control plane; we run a handoff playbook to minimize integration risk."
- Objection: "Latency spikes will kill our UX during holidays."
  - Quick reply: "Routing policies + fallback model variants preserve availability; we can simulate holiday spikes during pilot."

Slide 7 — Triage matrix (when a pilot starts to wobble)
- Symptoms: rising tail latency, KV eviction increase, tokenization mismatch, cold-start spikes.
- Quick traces to collect: 90/95/99 latencies, cache hit ratio by prefix, request size distribution, model version histogram.
- Rapid mitigations (order): 1) pin model variant, 2) enable prefix caching, 3) adjust batch window, 4) failover routing to lower-cost but compatible variant.

Slide 8 — Field script (60s opener for SEs)
- Intro: "We help teams turn prototype predictability into predictable run costs. Before we change your stack, we first quantify where the convex costs are coming from."
- Qualifier Qs (3):
  1) "What % of calls involve >1k tokens?"
  2) "How often do you see request bursts vs. steady throughput?"
  3) "Do you track cache reuse or session affinity today?"
- Close: "If you can share a week of anonymized request logs we can give a targeted improvement plan in two weeks."

Slide 9 — Pilot success rubric (scoring)
- Pilot momentum score (0-10) components:
  - Integration speed (0-3)
  - Measured unit-cost delta (0-3)
  - SLO adherence during canary (0-2)
  - Product team buy-in (0-2)
- Threshold: 7+ to recommend reserved capacity conversation.

Slide 10 — Handoff checklist for internal ops (SE -> Solutions Eng)
- Deliverables from pilot: baseline trace pack, regression eval set, rollback plan, recommended quantization profile, routing policy JSON, and cost-model snapshot.
- Who does what: ops-runbook owner (customer), se-point, solutions-eng reviewer.

Appendix — Mini battlecards and play snippets
- Quick flip: "Cost-first account" (script): empathize on unit economics, show sample month-by-month runway with and without optimizations.
- Quick flip: "Latency-first account": emphasize tail latency controls, SLO simulator anecdote, and option for dedicated pool.
- Quick technical follow-up list for PMs: 1) expected sequence lengths, 2) mean/peak throughput, 3) use of streaming vs. full response, 4) current model family and quantization tolerance.

Operational notes (internal):
- Risk flags: teams without request logs or strict NDA constraints are higher friction; consider a shorter, observability-first engagement.
- Next steps for this deck: convert to 6-slide field pack + one-page battlecard PDF.
- TODOs: get SLO simulator screenshots from SRE team, update pilot credit wording with finance, run one dry-run with SEs in EMEA timezone.

Field-ready snippets (copyable)
- 30s email opener: "Hi <name>, we’ve run similar pilots that uncover 30–60% hidden serving spend caused by cache churn and inefficient batching. Can we baseline one week of anonymized traffic and share a targeted plan? — Maya"

Notes-to-self:
- Use term 'convexity' sparingly — it's an internal framing for sellers, not for customer-facing slides without explanation.
- Keep numbers conservative and always attach the baseline assumptions.

End of sketch.
